_about: Every language we plan to offer. status: live | planned | pending. flag = ISO country code of the flag to show (flags/<code>.svg is made from it). group = country the language is grouped under on the home page (tiles are ordered by group, then by English name).

languages.name: বাংলা (বাংলাদেশ)
languages.note: Own translation (the Bangladeshi Bangla file): NOT the same text as bn. Second Bengali tile with the Bangladesh flag (confirmed). Audio made with a native Bangladesh-accent Narakeet voice (Mahiya/Salman). Section 4's long name wraps to three lines on a 320px phone: fine.

languages.name: فارسی
languages.note: Persian (colloquial register); audio made with a native Persian Narakeet voice (Shohreh/Reza). The doubled 'small' in the intro was resolved to the colloquial کوچیک. The 20 standard strings are drafts: have a Persian speaker check them.

languages.name: Português (Brasil)
languages.note: Built from the translator's file labelled 'Portuguese (Brazil)'. Two European words were changed to Brazilian in the text (intro yellow legend line: ligeiro -> leve; question 2 title: Vaga de calor -> Onda de calor). Audio recorded by the owner with a Brazilian voice (Claude cannot verify accents); the intro and question 2 clips were recorded BEFORE those two words changed, so they may still say the old words until re-recorded (2-row sheet provided). The 20 standard strings and the three new interface strings are Brazilian drafts by Claude: have a Brazilian speaker check them.

languages.name: Português (Portugal)
languages.note: Planned (second tile, decided 13 Oct 2026: Brazil first, Portugal later). Same translation with the translator's ORIGINAL wording (ligeiro, vaga de calor), European standard strings (drafts in tools/common_strings.json: secção, registo, Compreendo) and its OWN recording with a EUROPEAN Narakeet voice (the 22-row sheet is in portuguese-sheets.zip). Build with tools/make_template.py --code pt, then tools/apply_new_ui_strings.py.

languages.name: اردو
languages.note: Urdu (rtl, Pakistan flag). The six section headings were missing from the translator's file and were WRITTEN BY CLAUDE at the owner's request: a native speaker must check them. The first Narakeet run (non-Urdu voice) gave one tiny blip per sentence; the second run with a native Urdu voice (Mawra/Imran) and plain sheets worked. Urdu is traditionally written in Nastaliq; the default font is Naskh.

languages.name: नेपाली
languages.note: Nepali; audio made with a native Nepali Narakeet voice (Lhakpa/Tenzing). The English word 'step' in the intro was replaced with चरणहरू. Nepal's non-rectangular flag renders correctly. The 20 standard strings are drafts: have a Nepali speaker check them.

languages.name: 客家話
languages.note: Written in traditional Chinese characters; no text-to-speech voice exists, so the audio was recorded by a Hakka speaker (long pauses capped at 0.7 s). Flag/country China: confirmed by the owner.

languages.name: 圍頭話
languages.note: Written Chinese (Cantonese-style); no text-to-speech voice exists, so the audio was recorded by a speaker (long pauses capped at 0.7 s). Flag/country China: confirmed by the owner. The 20 standard strings reuse the Cantonese wording: have a Weitou speaker check them.

languages.name: 潮州話
languages.note: Written in traditional Chinese; no text-to-speech voice exists, so the audio was recorded by a speaker (used exactly as sent). Flag/country China: provisional, please confirm.

languages.name: العربية الخليجية
languages.note: Gulf (Khaleeji) Arabic, written as the translator speaks it (colloquial: شقد, وايد, the feminine ـج ending, بچي), addressed to women. Right-to-left, tag ar-AE. UAE flag/country is PROVISIONAL (the dialect spans UAE, Kuwait, Qatar, Bahrain, Oman and eastern Saudi): the owner to confirm. Audio made by the owner with a Narakeet Emirati voice (Claude cannot verify accents; the owner chose between the AS-WRITTEN and the CH-RESPELLED sheets: which one was used is not recorded). Spelling to check: يأثر (twice) is normally يؤثر; 'your doctor' is دكتورتك in the intro but دكتورتج elsewhere. The 20 standard strings and the 3 new interface strings are drafts by Claude: have a Khaleeji speaker check them.
